name: Bane of Hope

facts.text: Level 81, 100,000 health. Casts Essense of Souls (damage over time). Its teleport of a target to one of three fixed spots is behind EpicEncounterMechanics.AllowDisplacement, which is off in Living Server.

story:
Every gaol needs a keeper whose work is not to hold the prisoners but to make them stop believing in the door. In Caer Sidi that was the Bane of Hope. Arawn did not make it cruel; he made it thorough. In the old days of the gaol it moved those who came near it, without warning, to the far ends of the fortress, so that men who had planned an escape together woke three halls apart and alone, and while they searched for each other it burned their souls.

It did not turn when the gaol rose, nor did it stay loyal. It went on with its work on prisoner and rebel alike, and in the first seasons after the rising it did the same to Albion. It scattered Dame Nest's company through four tiers of the dead, and it moved Brother Cadoc three halls away from Dame Ysolde's side in the dark.

Then Ysolde's company broke it, and when it stood again at its post, it had forgotten how to move a man. The Inconnu say the part of it that cast people away was the part that believed they would come back, and that it died the first time someone did. Since that day the Bane of Hope has only burned. Its fire is a sickness of the soul that does its work slowly, and kills unless the prayers come quickly and keep coming. The prisoners still avoid its crossing, from habit, and the halls round it are quieter than most. Brother Cadoc wrote four words across the top of the page that tells of it: there is a door.
legend: In the first seasons it threw people across Caer Sidi to one of three spots, and every old guide is full of advice about walking back slowly. Forget that here: it does not port anyone any more. What is left is Essense of Souls, a heavy magic burn that ticks on whoever it picks and kills if nobody heals through it. Healers watch the burn and do not let it run; the rest of the raid stands and fights it where it is. It is a plain fight now, and the danger is a lazy healer, not a lost raider. Old Albion raids still keep a priest in the middle of the room out of habit, and nobody minds, because that is where the burn gets healed anyway. The prisoners avoid its crossing, so the halls round it are quiet: a good place to rest before the climb to Fate's Chosen. Keep a priest near the middle of the room so whoever comes walking back has a heal waiting. Never send the main tank to fetch a lost raider. Let them come home on their own feet, slowly, and call out every hall they pass.

loremasterTopic.text: The keeper whose work was to make prisoners stop believing in the door. In the gaol's old days it cast those near it to the far ends of the fortress; since Dame Ysolde's company broke it, it only burns their souls. See [caer sidi].

bookPage: The Bane of Hope did not seem to fight us so much as rearrange us. One moment Brother Cadoc was at my shoulder; the next he was gone, and I heard later that he had stood up three halls away in the dark with the dead turning to look at him, and had walked back to us slowly, praying aloud the whole way, and had woken nothing. Others were less calm. Dame Ysolde said afterwards that its burning was the lesser cruelty. The greater is that it makes you believe you are alone. We were not. That is how we won.
